title: Supreme Court Upholds Setting Aside of Shreeram Builders' Award, Orders Refund With 9% Interest
case_name: Shreeram Builders v. Upendra Kantilal Thanawala & Others
citation: Civil Appeal Nos. 9817-9818 of 2024, decided 29 October 2026
card_summary: The Supreme Court upheld the Bombay High Court's order setting aside an arbitral award that had directed landowners to execute a sale deed in Shreeram Builders' favour. The tribunal's order ignored the agreement's own conditions, and its price calculation was arbitrary. Rather than leave the builder with nothing, the Court used Article 142 to order a refund of every amount received, with 9 per cent interest.
card_tip: An arbitral tribunal awarding specific performance must still keep to the contract's own price and payment conditions; a tribunal that rewrites those terms risks the award being set aside under Section 34.
verification_notes: Confirmed by multiple independent reports (LiveLawBiz, SupremeToday, LawChakra, Lawtrend and others) agreeing on parties, citation, bench (Justices Sanjay Kumar and Sanjeev Sachdeva) and relief; judgment itself not accessed.
